newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 13.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Thursday:

* U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and his G7 allies want to rein in the dollar, but a sentence they included in their statement backing this goal may have unintentionally given traders reason to push the dollar even higher.
* Mutual fund investors poured about $24 billion into equity funds in January, the fourth-largest total on record.
* AMR's American Airlines canceled nearly all its overseas flights for Friday night as Saturday's deadline for a labor strike neared.
* Officials at vacation spots served by American said the economies in their regions could be hard hit by a strike.
* ITT Corp's board rejected Hilton Hotels hostile $6.5 billion bid, setting up what could be a lengthy battle.
* The Dow industrials surged 103.52 points to 6,961.63, the largest gain of the year.
* Treasury prices ended lower, following poor results at an auction of 10-year notes.
* Michael Boskin is releasing the results of a survey of fellow economists to back his conclusion that the Consumer Price Index overstates inflation.
* American workers' wage gains last year were the largest since 1990, keeping them ahead of inflation for only the second time in a decade, and economists expect the trend to continue.

* Europe made a last-minute decision to postpone its legal challenge to America's trade sanctions against Cuba, avoiding a breach with the United States that could threaten the World Trade Organization.
* The White House said it would let American news agencies open bureuas in Cuba for the first time in decades.
* Campbell Soup is celebrating the 100th anniversary of its condensed soup with ads pushing soup sold in glass jars.
* Canadian researchers have concluded that talking on a cellular phone while driving creates a risk of accidents as great as driving slightly drunk.

* Boris Berezovsky, one of Russia's richest businessmen and stormiest politicians, has filed a suit against Forbes magazine accusing it of defaming him by linking him to shady business deals and the murder of a young journalist.
* The trial of three members of Venezuela's Orlando Castro Llanes family, accused of fraud in the collapse of their financial empire, goes to a Manhattan jury tomorrow.
* Regulators ordered NYNEX to return $109.6 billion to its customers for what they say are shoddy service and improper business practices.

* Although the merger of NYNEX and Bell Atlantic is being touted as a combination of equals, the resignation of NYNEX executive Richard Jalkut makes it clear that Bell's senior executives will play a dominant role.

* Since America Online reported its quarterly results last Thursday, analysts are raising new questions about how costly the company's business strategy is proving to be, whether it has the cash to execute its plans and how long it will take for the company to show steady profits.
-- New York newsdesk 212-859-1610.
